title: KKR European Infrastructure RAIF — CSSF 10% AML/KYC Beneficial Ownership Look-Through
initialRequestBrief: Luxembourg counsel to KKR European Infrastructure RAIF III SCSp issued Revision 2 of the fund's AML/KYC pack at 08:40 CEST on 29 September 2025, 48 hours before the initial close on 1 October. For investors with high-risk jurisdiction exposure and for multi-tier holding structures, the beneficial-ownership threshold drops from more than 25% to 10% or more, with recursive look-through up to four tiers. The AIFM's compliance team says it applies to the initial close. UAT was signed off on 26 September, 31 investor drafts are in progress and 12 subscriptions are already signed. The sponsor will not move the close date.
summary: Two days before go-live, Luxembourg counsel lowered the UBO disclosure threshold from 25% to 10% with four-tier look-through for high-risk and multi-tier investors. A parameterised recursive look-through schema plus an in-place draft migration kept the initial close on time without restarting any investor.
howItWent: The v1 form had a static three-row UBO table, one look-through row per entity and 25% hard-coded in validation, so counsel's Revision 2 was a structural rewrite rather than a number change. David Le replaced it overnight with a recursive four-tier repeater driven by parameters: the threshold, its comparator, the in-scope investor types and the depth, each changed through an audited entry. A versioned migration moved all 31 in-flight drafts with no data loss, leaving 24 untouched and re-prompting 7 for 19 additional owner rows only, as the pack's transitional clause (Section 7.2(a)) allowed. QA's first run caught a migration bug where v1 look-through rows typed as natural persons actually held entity names; those were flagged for re-confirmation instead. The walk-through with the AIFM's compliance team and counsel gave a GO, the initial close held at 09:00 Lux on 1 October, and the one investor with a Tier 4 holding company still over threshold was escalated and moved to the subsequent closing.
resolutionSteps: Build a 4-tier recursive UBO ownership look-through compliance checklist: a recursive repeater whose children open only when an entity meets the applicable threshold below Tier 4, with effective percentages multiplied down the chain.

Parameterize the AML threshold (25% standard exclusive vs. 10% inclusive strict look-through) and the in-scope investor types, so future funds toggle them with an audit entry instead of rebuilding forms.
Pin drafts to their schema version and ship a v1-to-v2 migration rule that keeps entered values and re-prompts only the new required owners.
Escalate a Tier 4 legal person still over threshold to the AIFM's compliance officer with a certified structure chart instead of adding a fifth tier.
Ask Luxembourg counsel at kickoff about pending AML/KYC changes and secure a transitional clause for in-flight subscriptions.

pitfalls.warning: Never hard-code a regulatory threshold or encode it as a fixed number of table rows; the row count is the threshold in disguise.
pitfalls.author: sarah.tran

pitfalls.warning: Flipping the threshold in place on a published schema makes every half-filled in-scope draft fail validation on its next save. Version the schema and migrate.
pitfalls.author: david.le

pitfalls.warning: The comparator travels with the number: "more than 25%" is exclusive, "10% or more" is inclusive. Test x-0.01, x and x+0.01.
pitfalls.author: david.le

pitfalls.warning: v1 look-through rows typed NATURAL_PERSON may actually name entities; flag them for re-confirmation during migration rather than guessing.
pitfalls.author: sarah.tran

artifacts.description: Counsel's Revision 2 AML/KYC text (high-risk exposure, multi-tier structures, 10% four-tier look-through, transitional clause, Annex C worked example) plus Anduin's parameter-by-parameter reuse guidance.
Recursive four-tier UBO look-through form schema with parameterised threshold, comparator, scope toggle and depth, audit trail, depth escalation and the v1-to-v2 draft migration.
